title: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem
body:
Read the chapter → [Zechariah 8](/bible/zechariah/8)

## Introduction

This session covers Zechariah 8 through 11. The teaching runs on one line the whole way: the promises here are made to Israel and to no other nation, and the bible defines its own terms, so Zion, my people, and the remnant are each proved out of the scriptures themselves. From there it goes to the judgment on the nations that had a hand in the captivity, the King coming lowly and riding upon an ass, and the shepherds who were supposed to feed the flock and did not.

**[Zechariah 8:1-3](/bible/zechariah/8#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/zechariah/8#v1)</sup> Again the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/zechariah/8#v2)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I was jealous for her with great fury.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/zechariah/8#v3)</sup> Thus saith the Lord; I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth; and the mountain of the Lord of hosts the holy mountain.

- I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I was jealous for her with great fury.
- I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth; and the mountain of the Lord of hosts the holy mountain.
- The bible has its own definition for the words written in it. Zion is named plainly, so there is no need to guess who he is jealous over and who he returns to.

  Precepts:
  - **[Zephaniah 3:14](/bible/zephaniah/3#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/zephaniah/3#v14)</sup> Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.

    Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel. The daughter of Zion is Israel.

**[Zechariah 8:6](/bible/zechariah/8#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/zechariah/8#v4)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/zechariah/8#v5)</sup> And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/zechariah/8#v6)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith the Lord of hosts.

- There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age.
- The streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof. That cannot be done in this captivity; it waits on the Most High to return us to our own land.
- If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith the Lord of hosts.

**[Zechariah 8:7-8](/bible/zechariah/8#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/zechariah/8#v7)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country;
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/zechariah/8#v8)</sup> And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.

- Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; and I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem.
- They shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness. He is called the God of Israel because he is the God of that people and none else.
- My people is not a loose term in the scriptures. It is named.

  Precepts:
  - **[Matthew 2:6](/bible/matthew/2#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/matthew/2#v6)</sup> And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.

    Out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.

**[Zechariah 8:12](/bible/zechariah/8#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/zechariah/8#v9)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words by the mouth of the prophets, which were in the day that the foundation of the house of the Lord of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/zechariah/8#v10)</sup> For before these days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction: for I set all men every one against his neighbour.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/zechariah/8#v11)</sup> But now I will not be unto the residue of this people as in the former days, saith the Lord of hosts.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/zechariah/8#v12)</sup> For the seed shall be prosperous; the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things.

- Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words by the mouth of the prophets, which were in the day that the foundation of the house of the Lord of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built.
- Before these days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction.
- But now I will not be unto the residue of this people as in the former days, saith the Lord of hosts. The seed shall be prosperous; the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things.
- The remnant that possesses these things is named in the prophets, and it is the children of Israel. This is why the bible must be read precept upon precept, because people hear my people and think it means all nations.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 10:22](/bible/isaiah/10#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/isaiah/10#v22)</sup> For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.

    For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return.

**[Zechariah 8:13](/bible/zechariah/8#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/zechariah/8#v13)</sup> And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing: fear not, but let your hands be strong.

- As ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing: fear not, but let your hands be strong.
- Both houses are named, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom.
- The curse among the heathen is the curse written in the law, and the blessing is the same blessing promised there for keeping the commandments.
- There is nowhere in the scriptures where the Most High says he will save another nation to give them the kingdom. Israel is the one who needs a saviour, and the condition we are in is why.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:37](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v37)**
    > <sup>[37](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v37)</sup> And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.

    Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.
  - **[Luke 1:68-71](/bible/luke/1#v68)**
    > <sup>[68](/bible/luke/1#v68)</sup> Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people,
    >
    > <sup>[69](/bible/luke/1#v69)</sup> And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David;
    >
    > <sup>[70](/bible/luke/1#v70)</sup> As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began:
    >
    > <sup>[71](/bible/luke/1#v71)</sup> That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us;

    Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, that we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us.
  - **[Luke 1:72-74](/bible/luke/1#v72)**
    > <sup>[72](/bible/luke/1#v72)</sup> To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant;
    >
    > <sup>[73](/bible/luke/1#v73)</sup> The oath which he sware to our father Abraham,
    >
    > <sup>[74](/bible/luke/1#v74)</sup> That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear,

    To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant, the oath which he sware to our father Abraham, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear.

**[Zechariah 8:19](/bible/zechariah/8#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/zechariah/8#v14)</sup> For thus saith the Lord of hosts; As I thought to punish you, when your fathers provoked me to wrath, saith the Lord of hosts, and I repented not:
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/zechariah/8#v15)</sup> So again have I thought in these days to do well unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: fear ye not.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/zechariah/8#v16)</sup> These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates:
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/zechariah/8#v17)</sup> And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the Lord.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/zechariah/8#v18)</sup> And the word of the Lord of hosts came unto me, saying,
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/zechariah/8#v19)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore love the truth and peace.

- As I thought to punish you, when your fathers provoked me to wrath, and I repented not; so again have I thought in these days to do well unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: fear ye not.
- These are the things that ye shall do: speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates.
- Let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the Lord.
- The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore love the truth and peace.

**[Zechariah 8:23](/bible/zechariah/8#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/zechariah/8#v20)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; It shall yet come to pass, that there shall come people, and the inhabitants of many cities:
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/zechariah/8#v21)</sup> And the inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, Let us go speedily to pray before the Lord, and to seek the Lord of hosts: I will go also.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/zechariah/8#v22)</sup> Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the Lord.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/zechariah/8#v23)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.

- The inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, Let us go speedily to pray before the Lord, and to seek the Lord of hosts: I will go also.
- Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the Lord.
- Ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.
- The nations coming is not the nations receiving the kingdom. The prophets say what their coming looks like: Israel set in their own land, and the strangers joined to them and serving there.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 14:1-2](/bible/isaiah/14#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/isaiah/14#v1)</sup> For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/isaiah/14#v2)</sup> And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

    The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob; and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were.
